title: SoftBank in talks to buy US security group Allied Universal
source_used: The Japan Times (carrying Bloomberg's report), Channel NewsAsia via UA.NEWS; Reuters and Financial Times headlines seen
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 16 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that SoftBank Group is considering buying Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the US.
The deal could give privately held Allied an equity value of as much as $18 billion.
Allied also has about $12 billion of publicly traded debt (loans and bonds), which could bring the total deal value close to $30 billion, according to Bloomberg data.
Allied's backers include private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Canadian pension fund La Caisse.
Bloomberg ties the interest to founder Masayoshi Son's exploration of AI-powered robots across industries.

Per Channel NewsAsia's account of Bloomberg: talks are at an early stage with no final decisions, including on price; SoftBank declined to comment; Bloomberg's sources say SoftBank could in future replace some guards with robots but humanoid security workers would take more time.
The Financial Times headline (paywalled) says SoftBank is in talks to buy Allied; Reuters headline says SoftBank weighs an $18 billion acquisition, source says.
quote_evidence: SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the U.S., people familiar with the matter said, as founder Masayoshi Son explores ways to deploy AI-powered robots across industries.
The potential transaction may give closely held Allied an equity value of as much as $18 billion, said some of the people, who asked not to be identified because the deliberations are private.
According to Bloomberg, the discussions are at an early stage, and no final decisions on a potential deal, including its price, have yet been made.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI-focused investor weighing a purchase of the largest US security-guard employer, with robots named as a possible long-term replacement for some staff.
notes: FT original paywalled (no text). Read Bloomberg's text as carried by The Japan Times (only the first paragraphs are open) and Channel NewsAsia's summary of Bloomberg via UA.NEWS. Bloomberg published first (16 Oct 19:11 GMT), Reuters then FT (17 Oct 02:07 GMT); source credited to Bloomberg. Investing.com headline says deal up to $30 billion (equity plus debt), not used as the equity value.
